To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

We present the Tenth Data Release from SDSS-III, which includes the first public spectroscopic data from its APOGEE experiment, along with spectroscopic and photometric data from the BARYON OSCILLATION SPECTROSCOPIC SURVEY.
the APOGEE spectra are of high quality, and that the derived stellar parameters are accurate and precise.

the SDSS-III BOSS has obtained a large sample of galaxy redshifts that will be used for cosmological studies and the APOGEE has obtained a large set of high resolution infrared spectra of Milky Way stars that will be used to measure their metallicities and radial velocities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the formation history of the Milky Way by determining the chemical composition of its stellar components.
the development of a new type of data analysis system that will be capable of handling very large volumes of data.
the development and application of methods for the analysis of high dimensional data sets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DR10 includes spectroscopic data on 282,397 unique objects from APOGee and BOSS.
DR10 includes spectroscopic data on 617,399 objects, comprising 422,451 stars, 179,960 galaxies, and 14,988 quasars.
DR10 includes spectroscopic data on roughly 750,000 objects from 9385 deg2 of sky.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have provided the community with a spectroscopic data set that includes 80% of the sky, with the median fiber distance of 0.6 degrees, and with the typical signal to noise of 2 for galaxies and quasars and 40 for stars.
we have provided 1.6 million spectra, 2.3 million derived quantities (radial velocity, stellar parameters, etc.), and 100 million astrophysical objects.
the APOGEE and BOSS surveys have begun to produce high-quality data that represent significant advances in the field of large-scale spectroscopy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SDSS-III APOGEE and BOSS spectroscopic surveys are well underway and delivering spectra substantially faster than has been the case for previous SDSS releases.
we have been able to produce a catalog with 1.5 million spectra from the SDSS-III/BOSS survey.
the data release has a high degree of accuracy and precision, which is important for the study of the chemical composition of stars in the Milky Way.
